The A3 criterion requires sites to be >= 10.0 km from small airports/airstrips. [FACT] The Martinska power station is located at coordinates 49.059218°N, 18.907019°E in the Žilina region of Slovakia. [INFERENCE] This location is in the Váh River valley in north-central Slovakia, an area with mixed topography of valleys and hills. [UNKNOWN] Without access to comprehensive small airport databases or enrichment data, I cannot reliably identify or estimate distances to small airports, airstrips, or general aviation facilities in this specific area. The threshold of 10.0 km cannot be evaluated without site-specific airfield data.

The threshold requires sites to be ≥16.0 km from airports where annual flight operations exceed 500×d². [FACT] The Martinska power station is located in Martin, Slovakia (49.059°N, 18.907°E) in the Žilina region. [INFERENCE] The nearest significant airport is Žilina Airport (ILZ), approximately 25-30 km to the northwest, which is a small regional airport with minimal commercial traffic (<5,000 movements/year). [FACT] Slovakia's main airports are Bratislava (BTS, ~200 km south) and Košice (KSC, ~250 km east), both well beyond the 30 km assessment radius. At 25-30 km distance, even a major hub would need >312,500-450,000 movements/year to trigger the criterion, which no Central European airport outside of Frankfurt or Istanbul achieves. The estimated distance of 25-30 km to the nearest airport is well above the 16 km threshold, therefore the site passes this criterion.

The threshold for A2 is >= 7.5 km from Type 2 airports (military airfields with fast jets, heavy cargo airports, or operationally challenging airports). [FACT] The Martinska power station is located at 49.059218°N, 18.907019°E in the Žilina region of northern Slovakia. [INFERENCE] This location is in the Váh River valley area, approximately 15-20 km southeast of Žilina city. [ESTIMATE] The nearest known military airfield is likely Sliač Air Base (central Slovakia) at approximately 80-100 km distance, well beyond the 15 km assessment radius. [INFERENCE] The Žilina region primarily has civilian airports (Žilina Airport for general aviation), with no known active military airfields or heavy cargo operations within the immediate vicinity. The estimated distance to any potential Type 2 airport source is well above the 7.5 km threshold, therefore the criterion is satisfied.

The threshold requires >= 5.0 km distance from SEVESO III hazardous material facilities. [FACT] The Martinska power station is located in Žilina Region, Slovakia, at coordinates 49.059218°N, 18.907019°E. [INFERENCE] Based on the coordinates, this appears to be in the Kysuce valley area of northern Slovakia, which is primarily rural/small industrial rather than a major petrochemical zone. [UNKNOWN] However, I cannot identify specific SEVESO III facilities or their distances from this site without access to Slovak environmental authority databases or detailed industrial mapping. [ESTIMATE] The region is not known for major chemical plants or refineries (which are concentrated more in western Slovakia near Bratislava), suggesting the nearest SEVESO facility may be > 5 km, but this cannot be confirmed from available information. Slovakia's SEVESO register would be required for definitive assessment.

The A8 criterion requires sites to be >= 8.0 km from sources capable of producing drifting hazardous clouds. [FACT] The Martinska power station is located at coordinates 49.059218°N, 18.907019°E in the Žilina region of Slovakia. [INFERENCE] This location places the site in the Váh River valley in north-central Slovakia, an area with mixed industrial and agricultural activity. [UNKNOWN] Without enrichment data on nearby industrial facilities, chemical plants, major gas pipelines, or water treatment plants using bulk chlorine/ammonia, I cannot reliably estimate distances to potential cloud-forming sources. [INFERENCE] The Žilina region contains various industrial facilities and is crossed by major European gas pipeline systems, but I cannot determine specific locations or distances from this site. The estimated distance to hazardous cloud sources cannot be determined with sufficient reliability to compare against the 8.0 km threshold, therefore the assessment is inconclusive.

The A5 criterion requires sites to be ≥30 km from active military practice/bombing/firing ranges. [FACT] The Martinska power station is located at coordinates 49.059218°N, 18.907019°E in the Žilina region of northern Slovakia. [INFERENCE] This places the site in the Váh River valley area, approximately 15-20 km southeast of Žilina city. [UNKNOWN] No enrichment data was provided for military installation proximity, and I cannot identify specific active military ranges in this region of Slovakia with sufficient confidence. [FACT] Slovakia operates the Lešť military training area in central Slovakia and has various smaller military facilities, but the locations and current operational status of active firing ranges near the Žilina region are not well-documented in public sources. Without being able to identify and measure distances to specific active military ranges, I cannot determine whether the 30 km threshold is met. Military range data represents a critical information gap that requires specialized defense ministry sources or restricted airspace databases not available in this desk study.

The threshold for ammunition storage proximity is 8.0 km. [FACT] The Martinska power station is located in Martin, Žilina Region, Slovakia at coordinates 49.059218°N, 18.907019°E. [INFERENCE] Slovakia maintains several military installations as a NATO member state, and the region around Martin has historical military significance from the Soviet era. However, [UNKNOWN] I cannot identify specific ammunition storage facilities or major military bases within 15 km of this site with sufficient confidence. [ESTIMATE] While there may be military installations in the broader Žilina region, I cannot determine their precise locations, nature, or whether they include ammunition storage without access to classified military infrastructure data. Given that ammunition storage facilities are among the most sensitive military assets with extremely poor public data coverage, and the precautionary principle must apply for exclusionary safety criteria, this assessment requires field verification and consultation with Slovak military authorities.

[FACT] The Martinska power station is located at 49.059°N, 18.907°E in the Žilina region of Slovakia. [FACT] This places the site in the Western Carpathians tectonic unit, specifically in the northern part of Slovakia near the Polish border. [INFERENCE] Based on the ESHM20 seismic hazard model, this region of Slovakia typically experiences PGA values in the range of 0.10-0.20g at 475-year return period, well below the 0.5g threshold for NuScale VOYGR-6 design basis. [ESTIMATE] The estimated PGA at 475-year return period is approximately 0.15g ± 0.05g, which is significantly below the 0.5g threshold, therefore the site passes the seismic ground motion avoidance criterion with substantial margin.

[FACT] The Martinska power station is located at coordinates 49.059218°N, 18.907019°E in the Žilina region of Slovakia, which places it in the northern interior of Slovakia. [FACT] Slovakia is a landlocked country in Central Europe with no coastline, located over 400 km from the nearest sea (Adriatic Sea to the south). [INFERENCE] The site coordinates place it in the Váh River valley system, a typical location for Slovak thermal power plants, which are inland river-cooled facilities. The threshold requires the site to satisfy at least one condition: (a) ≥10 km from sea/ocean shore, (b) ≥1 km from lake/fjord shore (lakes >10 km long), or (c) ≥50 m elevation above nearest mean water level. The estimated distance to the nearest sea is >400 km, which vastly exceeds the 10 km threshold. Therefore, condition (a) is satisfied with enormous margin, making tsunami exposure impossible at this inland location.

The threshold for A11 requires adequate flood protection for the design-basis flood (10,000-year return period), with practical indicators including site elevation ≥5 m above 100-year flood level. [FACT] The Martinska power station is located in Žilina Region, Slovakia, at coordinates 49.059°N, 18.907°E. [INFERENCE] Based on the coordinates, this site is in the Váh River valley system in northern Slovakia, where most thermal power plants were historically sited for cooling water access. [UNKNOWN] Critical data gaps prevent assessment: site elevation is unknown, cooling water source is unspecified, and no enrichment data on flood zone classification is available. [ESTIMATE] The Váh River basin has experienced significant flood events (notably 1997, 2010), but without knowing the site's elevation relative to the river or its position within the floodplain, flood risk cannot be determined. The 32 MWe lignite plant operated from 1962-2020, suggesting some flood resilience over nearly 60 years, but this provides insufficient evidence for nuclear design-basis flood protection. Desk study verification of topographic maps, flood hazard maps, and site elevation data would be required to complete this assessment.

The threshold for grid adequacy is >= 220 kV transmission capable of exporting 462 MWe. [FACT] The Martinska power station had an installed capacity of only 32 MWe, which is far below the 462 MWe requirement for the NuScale VOYGR-6 SMR. [INFERENCE] A 32 MWe lignite plant would typically have been connected to the distribution grid at 22-110 kV level, not the high-voltage transmission system required for 462 MWe export. [ESTIMATE] The existing grid connection is approximately 14 times smaller than needed (32 vs 462 MWe), indicating substantial transmission infrastructure upgrades would be required. While Slovakia has a well-developed transmission grid operated by SEPS, this specific site's connection was sized for a much smaller plant and would need major reinforcement.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Martinska power station is located in Martin, Slovakia, a regional center in Žilina Region with established transport infrastructure. [INFERENCE] As a lignite-fired power plant operating from 1962-2020, this facility would have required substantial coal deliveries over its 58-year operational life, indicating robust transport access was historically available. [FACT] Martin is connected to Slovakia's rail network via the main Bratislava-Košice railway line, and [ESTIMATE] the nearest rail connection is likely within 1-2 km of the plant site given typical coal plant siting practices. [FACT] The D1 motorway (part of European route E75) passes near Martin, providing heavy road transport capability within approximately 5 km. The combination of mainline rail access (suitable for multi-car 700t module transport) and motorway access (suitable for segmented module delivery) clearly exceeds the threshold requirement of at least one capable transport mode.
